verified: The report is a Hacker News submission dated 26 November 2026 titled "AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp", linking to devnull.land/amd-specific-llama-cpp, and it is presented as an AMD-targeted fork of llama.cpp; the submission itself carries no README, benchmark, version or license text in what was supplied. The comments describe other people's separate AMD-focused forks and tuning work (gfx906 cards, an MI100 ROCm kernel port, an R9700 setup), not the contents of this fork.
unconfirmed: What this fork changes relative to upstream llama.cpp, which AMD architectures it targets, any measured speedup, its license, and whether it is installable today. The performance figures in the comments — 2400 tok/s prefill and 150 tok/s decode on an R9700, "1 TB/s" HBM2 datacenter cards for $200, tripled Qwen 3.8 speeds on an M1 port — are commenters' own claims about their own setups and were not independently checked.

verified: Hacker News 于 2026 年 11 月 26 日出现一篇题为「AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp」的帖子（发布者 julianlam），链接指向 devnull.land 上的介绍页；评论区多位开发者分别表示，自己为 AMD 显卡（gfx906 系列、MI100、R9700 等）维护或使用 llama.cpp 的优化分支。
unconfirmed: 该 fork 究竟改动了什么、支持哪些显卡与 ROCm 版本、有无可复现的性能数据、以何种许可证发布，现有报道均无法核实——介绍页正文未提供。评论中「32GB、约 1 TB/s 带宽的 gfx906 显卡仅约 200 美元」「R9700 单卡 prefill 2400 tok/s、decode 150 tok/s」等数字，是个人用户对各自项目的说法，并非对该 fork 的独立测试。
